Description: Move around the filesystem and create, copy, delete and inspect files and folders.
Read files in the terminal, page through output, compare files and edit text.
Find files anywhere on the system and locate where commands live.
Filter, cut, transform and sort text coming from files or other commands.
Chain commands, decide where output and errors go, and run things in the background.
Check who you are, switch users, and manage accounts, passwords and groups.
Control who can read, write and run files, plus special attributes and capabilities.
Shell settings, environment variables, aliases and handy history shortcuts.
See what's running, limit or repeat commands, and schedule jobs with cron.
Network interfaces, open ports and sockets, and raw connections with netcat.
Connect to remote machines and manage SSH keys.
Inspect binary data, convert between formats, hash files and work with archives.
Update the system, manage packages and check system info.
Version control: clone projects, explore history, work with branches and publish changes.
